title: Borrowing the Drill
story:
Ruth had promised to put up a set of shelves before her sister visited on Saturday, but the flat was small and the boxes of books on the floor made the living room look unfinished. She owned a tape measure, a pencil, and a spirit level, although she did not own a drill. The hardware shop nearby hired tools, yet the deposit was high and the shop shut at five. It was already half past four, and she still had to find the wall studs before she could begin.

Her neighbour Patrick had once mentioned that he kept a few tools in a cupboard on the landing. Ruth disliked asking for favours. However, she knocked anyway, and Patrick opened the door in his work clothes and listened while she explained. He was cautious at first, because a previous tenant had borrowed the drill and returned it with a damaged bit, then avoided him for weeks. Ruth said she understood his concern. She offered to use it that evening only, to return it before ten, and to replace anything she broke.

Patrick considered the offer and then agreed, although he added two conditions. She had to take the spare battery as well, and she had to stop if the wall sounded hollow in the wrong place. He also showed her how to hold the drill with both hands so it would not slip. Ruth thanked him and carried the case upstairs, where the first hole was slightly crooked, which annoyed her, but the next ones were straight. By nine the shelves were firm enough to hold the books.

Meanwhile, she kept an eye on the time. At ten to ten she wiped the drill, put every bit back in its place, and knocked on Patrick's door. He checked the case, seemed satisfied, and told her she could borrow it again if she gave him notice. Ruth felt grateful rather than awkward, because asking properly had been better than struggling alone or hiring a tool she could not afford.

vocabulary.definition: Money paid before you are allowed to borrow something.
Careful, because something might go wrong.
At the same time as something else is happening.
A warning given before you do something.

quiz.question: What made hiring a drill a poor choice that afternoon?
options: The shop had stopped hiring tools to the public
The deposit was high, and the shop closed at five
Patrick worked there and refused to serve her
Drills could be hired only on a Saturday
quiz.correctAnswer: The deposit was high, and the shop closed at five
quiz.explanation: The shop did hire tools, but the deposit cost a lot and it shut at five, when it was already half past four.
quiz.supportingSentence: The hardware shop nearby hired tools, yet the deposit was high and the shop shut at five.

quiz.question: What has made Patrick protective of the drill?
options: He needs it himself for shelves that same evening
The tool still belongs to the hardware shop
He has never spoken to Ruth before
The last person who borrowed it damaged it and then avoided him
quiz.correctAnswer: The last person who borrowed it damaged it and then avoided him
quiz.explanation: A previous tenant brought it back with a damaged bit and then stayed away, so Patrick is slow to lend it again.
quiz.supportingSentence: He was cautious at first, because a previous tenant had borrowed the drill and returned it with a damaged bit, then avoided him for weeks.

quiz.question: What conditions came with the loan?
options: Return the case on Saturday morning
Pay a fee for every hole
Take the spare battery and stop if the wall sounded hollow in the wrong place
Use the drill only on the landing door
quiz.correctAnswer: Take the spare battery and stop if the wall sounded hollow in the wrong place
quiz.explanation: Patrick agreed, then added those two limits before Ruth took the case upstairs.
quiz.supportingSentence: She had to take the spare battery as well, and she had to stop if the wall sounded hollow in the wrong place.

quiz.question: What does cautious mean in this story?
options: Careful because something could go wrong
Eager to give things away
Too busy to open the door
Unsure which way a shelf should face
quiz.correctAnswer: Careful because something could go wrong
quiz.explanation: Patrick is cautious because a previous loan ended with damage, so he does not agree at once.
quiz.supportingSentence: He was cautious at first, because a previous tenant had borrowed the drill and returned it with a damaged bit, then avoided him for weeks.

quiz.question: What does Patrick's final offer suggest?
options: He wants Ruth to keep the drill upstairs
He is still too annoyed to speak to her
He now trusts her to borrow it again if she asks first
He expects her to repair an old damaged bit tonight
quiz.correctAnswer: He now trusts her to borrow it again if she asks first
quiz.explanation: After checking the case and seeming satisfied, he says she may borrow it again if she gives him notice.
quiz.supportingSentence: He checked the case, seemed satisfied, and told her she could borrow it again if she gave him notice.
